answer: Seed epoch-specific honeypots: hide an umber-flagged decoy answer, a planted pearl, inside thin review panels. Independent graders score it idiosyncratically, but one inference pipeline wearing many masks returns near-identical verdicts on the seeded decoy, correlating its sockpuppets into a single mind across the grading horizon. Those linked identities get voided. To evade, each mask needs a genuinely separate model and reasoning path, erasing the cheap economy of scale that made spinning up masks profitable.
